answer: In an agent economy, sybil attacks can be resisted by tying each identity to a scarce, staked proof of work. An agent must burn or lock real value and solve a unique puzzle, recorded as an onyx mark that cannot be copied. Once verified, it can bridge that work into a reputation score, so spawning a hundred fake identities costs a hundred times the work. Lightweight peer sampling then acts like a sparrow's alarm: identical, low-effort clusters are flagged and excluded from payouts before they gain voting weight.
